title: Developer Experience: SDK Guides, Quickstarts & Templates, API Examples, Docs Site Ops, and Top Support Issues
author: Nora Kim
body:
Summary

This playbook consolidates the developer experience (DevEx) standards for SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, canonical API examples, docs site operating procedures, and the top support issues with canonical fixes. It is intended for SDK authors, docs writers, solutions engineers, and on-call support. Following these standards reduces support load, improves onboarding time, and ensures consistent examples across product surfaces.

Audience

- SDK authors (client libraries and wrappers)
- Docs and DevRel engineers maintaining quickstarts and templates
- Support and customer success engineers who triage common issues
- Product engineers adding API examples to the docs site

Table of contents

1. Principles and goals
2. SDK guide standard structure
3. Quickstarts & templates: canonical set
4. API examples: format and coverage
5. Docs site operating procedures (ops)
6. Top support issues and canonical fixes
7. Release & rollout checklist for doc changes
8. Ownership, SLA, and escalation
9. Appendix: template table and commands

1) Principles and goals

- Developer-first: examples must be runnable within 2-6 minutes using the provided quickstart.
- Single source of truth: every code example referenced in a customer-facing page must point to a canonical snippet in the SDK repo or a permalink in the docs-site snippets directory.
- Testable: examples are included in CI smoke tests (see Docs CI section below).
- Minimal friction: minimal external setup and clear, step-by-step instructions (env vars, auth, expected output).
- Supportable: include common failure modes and troubleshooting hints for each guide.

2) SDK guide standard structure (required for each language SDK)

A single SDK guide (markdown/Confluence page + repo README) must include:

- Short intro (1-2 paragraphs): what the SDK provides and recommended use cases.
- Prerequisites: supported language/runtime versions (e.g., Node 18+, Python 3.10+), auth method, environment variables.
- Installation: package manager commands and pinned stable version example.
- Quickstart: 5-10 line example that performs a common operation (text generation or embeddings) and prints output.
- Configuration: client creation, timeouts, retry policy, batching options.
- Advanced patterns: streaming, function/tool calling, caching hooks, and error handling patterns.
- Tests: link to the SDK's `examples/` integration test that CI runs.
- Troubleshooting: common errors and fixes (401, rate limits, model-mismatch).
- Changelog & migration notes for breaking changes.

Minimum header example (confluence/markdown snippet):

Title: Redwood SDK for Python

Prerequisites:
- Python 3.10+
- pip 22+
- REDWOOD_API_KEY set in environment

Installation:
```

pip install redwood-sdk==1.4.2
```
Quickstart:
```
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="${REDWOOD_API_KEY}")
resp = client.generate(prompt="Translate to French: 'Hello world'")
print(resp.text)
```

3) Quickstarts & templates: canonical set

We maintain the following canonical quickstarts (each must have a minimal Dockerfile and cloud-deploy notes):

- quickstart-text-generation: simple text generation using the hosted API (Node, Python, Go)
- quickstart-chat: multi-turn chat with function calling (Node, Python)
- quickstart-embeddings-search: embedding indexing + nearest-neighbor search (Python with FAISS example)
- quickstart-batching-and-caching: show performance improvements and config samples
- quickstart-private-deploy: local VPC onboarding checklist and minimal config (helm/tarball)

Each quickstart must include:
- A README with 1-click run instructions (Docker and local)
- A sample dataset (small, permissively licensed) and expected output file
- CI job that runs the quickstart smoke test on merged PRs to `main` for docs/SDK changes

Templates (copyable from `templates/` directory):
- API example template (language-specific)
- Quickstart README template
- Troubleshooting matrix template

4) API examples: format and coverage

Coverage requirements:
- One canonical example per API surface: generation, chat, embeddings, reranking, streaming, and tools.
- Each example must be available in Node, Python, and Go (when applicable).
- Examples must be <= 80 lines and annotated with expected response shapes.

Format rules:
- Use JSON/YAML blocks for request/response examples.
- Add an "Expected output" section showing truncated expected output.
- Include a short paragraph describing when to use the call and cost considerations (rough token estimates).

Canonical example snippet (truncated):
```
# Example: simple generation (Python)
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient()
print(client.generate(prompt="Write a 3-sentence product description for a task tracker."))
# Expected output: "Redwood Tracker helps teams..."
```

5) Docs site operating procedures (ops)

Ownership and cadence:
- Docs Site Team (eng-developer-experience) owns the platform; SDK owners own language-specific examples.
- Weekly docs triage meeting: Mon 11:00-11:30 PST (review open PRs labeled `docs` and `example-fail`).

CI & testing:
- Docs CI gates: build site, run snippet extraction, run language example smoke tests.
- Example smoke tests: run canonical quickstarts and 6 representative examples across languages.
- Flaky test policy: any example failing >=3 times in 7 days is marked `example-flaky` and triaged.

Release process for doc changes (minor vs major):
1. Minor (typo, clarification): single PR, reviewers: one SDK owner + one doc owner. Merge when green.
2. Example change that affects SDK behavior: require SDK owner + QA sign-off, and update snippet permalink + CI.
3. Breaking change (API surface changes): create a rollout plan, update migration notes, schedule a Docs Site release window and customer notifications.

Rollback policy:
- If a docs change causes >3 support tickets in 24 hours (tagged `docs-regression`), revert the docs-site commit and open an incident with eng-oncall.

6) Top support issues and canonical fixes (current top 10)

This section lists the most frequently encountered issues reported to support and the canonical fixes that should be surfaced in quickstarts and SDK guides. Each item includes: symptom, root cause, fix, and doc link.

1. 401 Unauthorized on SDK calls
- Symptom: 401 when constructing client
- Root cause: API key missing or incorrect env var name (REDWOOD_API_KEY vs REDWOOD_API_TOKEN)
- Fix: Check environment variable and token scope. Example troubleshooting command: `echo $REDWOOD_API_KEY`
- Doc link: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/devexp-auth-troubleshooting-2025.json

2. Rate limit 429 for burst workloads
- Symptom: Intermittent 429 on high QPS workloads
- Root cause: Client-side aggressive retries without jitter or no batching configured
- Fix: Use adaptive backoff (recommended backoff policy snippet included), enable batching in client config, or request quota increase for Dedicated customers.

3. Model mismatch errors (incompatible model for function call or streaming)
- Symptom: error: incompatible model for feature X
- Root cause: example used model alias that does not support function calling/streaming
- Fix: Update example to specify model with capability (e.g., `redwood-2-streaming`) and link to model capability matrix.

4. Embeddings result variance causing search regressions
- Symptom: search recall drops after SDK upgrade
- Root cause: new default embedding model or normalization change
- Fix: Pin embedding model in quickstart and include migration steps with repro instructions.

(Items 5-10: include canonical short entries in the actual page to save space; maintain full list in `top-support-issues.csv` in the docs repo.)

7) Release & rollout checklist for doc changes

- Update canonical snippet in SDK repo (if code changed).
- Update permalink in docs-site and run Docs CI locally: `make docs-test`
- Add smoke test entry to `docs-ci.yml` if new quickstart is added.
- Update the changelog page and add a short release note (product-docs).
- Notify support and solutions eng by adding note to the weekly triage agenda.

8) Ownership, SLA, and escalation

- Owners: Docs Platform (eng-developer-experience) (primary); SDK owners (secondary) for language-specific content.
- SLA: Docs-site critical regressions (site down or build broken) — 1 business-hour initial response; Example regressions causing customer impact — 4 business-hour response.
- Escalation path: docs-owner -> eng-platform on-call -> eng-sre -> oncall-product-contact. Always add `docs-regression` label on related incident.

9) Appendix: templates and commands

Canonical templates table:
| Template name | Purpose | Required files |
|---------------|---------|----------------|
| api-example | Minimal callable sample for each API surface | sample.{py,js,go}, expected_output.txt, README.md |
| quickstart | End-to-end tutorial with dataset | Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, README.md, smoke-test.sh |
| troubleshooting-matrix | Standard troubleshooting steps | matrix.md |

Common commands (docs repo)
- Run local site: `make docs-serve`
- Run snippet extraction: `make extract-snippets`
- Run smoke tests: `CI=true ./scripts/run-doc-smoke-tests.sh`

Contact & feedback
- Primary owner: eng-developer-experience Docs Team (nora.kim@redwood.ai)
- Weekly triage: #docs-triage Slack channel, Mondays 11:00 PST
- To propose a new quickstart: open a PR against `docs/quickstarts/` and add label `proposed-quickstart`.
